body: P3 (reviewer confidence medium), declared, no code change. When `mise which` under env -i from / gives no answer, the fallback `command -v` searches the caller's PATH, so an activated virtualenv's `bin/python3` (a PATH entry, with or without VIRTUAL_ENV) is the python3 that gets linked. The reviewer reproduced it with a marker-writing python3 placed first on PATH and the fixture's failing fake mise: --apply returned 0 and the marker was written. The fallback is the pattern item 6 prescribes (orch-gate.sh: `mise which` under env -i, else `command -v`, with shim refusal), and the caller's PATH is the operator's own shell, not a checkout's file: a checkout reaches it only through a PATH entry the operator added. The VIRTUAL_ENV variable itself never reaches the run (env -i), and on the operator's machine mise answers python3 first. Named in report.md and the RESULT as a residual limit; owner for any advisory follow-up: dotfiles-T133-verdict-audit-pool-followup-a01.

P3 (low), declared. The env -i re-run is skipped when the caller already sets VERDICT_BIN and PATH to exactly `<VERDICT_BIN>:/usr/bin:/bin`; the rest of that caller's environment then stays. Only the caller can set both (it is how --loop's children keep the pinned context), so this is the operator choosing the context, not a checkout or a stray inherited VERDICT_BIN, which e2092549 made re-pin.

P3 (operational), declared. env -i keeps only HOME, TMPDIR, PRECHECK_REQUIRED, VERDICT_BIN and PATH, as orch-gate.sh does. --loop's `git fetch -q origin` then fails (exit 2) if origin needs SSH agent auth, and a uv cache moved by UV_CACHE_DIR or XDG_CACHE_HOME makes the offline PyYAML read empty, which holds conditions 5 and 8. Both fail closed. The Check's shadow run (validation §10) read GitHub through the pinned gh with this environment.

P3 (informational), declared by design. Tools resolve from / rather than the checkout root: the root is the checkout the --apply guard inspects, and its mise.toml lies outside the guarded directories, so resolving there would let that file pick a tool, which item 6 forbids. This repository's mise.toml has an empty [tools], so the choice changes nothing today.

P3 (style), declared. `echo ... >&2 && exit N` in the refusal loop, usage, stop and audit-pool.sh's usage keeps each on one line (shfmt expands `{ a; b; }`). With stderr closed the group fails and errexit or the ERR trap ends the run with exit 2, a hold, never an accept.

P3 (lint CI does not gate), declared. `ruff check` with the repository config reports I001 twice, RUF100 three times (the `noqa` comments name rules the config does not enable) and PLW1510 for `subprocess.run` without `check=` in run_in_repo (the explicit `check=False` was dropped to stay within 120 columns; `check` defaults to False, so behaviour is unchanged). The repository's gate is `ruff format --check`, which passes, and tests/unit already carries ruff-check findings.

One round on e2092549 by a fresh read-only general-purpose subagent, given the commit range and the task file, not the worker's conclusions. Verdict: correct, with no P0, P1 or P2 and the six P3 above. It reproduced red on 85a47229's scripts (6 tests, 22 failures, every spec-named subcase) and green at e2092549 (21 tests), checked that the test files are byte-identical between f760acff and e2092549 and that scripts/require-crit-review.py is unchanged, compared the retained tests case by case (assertion calls 27 to 35 in test_verdict.py, the 8 the new tests add; 25 to 25 in test_audit_pool.py), and measured the caps at 500 and 499 against 68f8a70a. No fix round followed. This is local process evidence, not the task-level audit or reviewer authentication.

P3 (high), fixed in f75cdc1f. d0fd7859's `rm -f -- json && refuse` would skip the refusal if rm failed. The reviewer's scenario (`--json <a directory>`) does not reach that line: the pre-run cleanup at line 153 removes the json path first and a directory makes it exit 1 under errexit, so a red test for it would not discriminate and was dropped. The line is now `rm -f -- json || true` and then `refuse ... 3`, so the refusal never depends on rm.

P3 (low), declared. The checker writes the decoded record to the retained path and the JSON masker rewrites it a moment later (one uv start-up). A pool killed in that window leaves an unmasked record under .orchestration/validation/ of the trusted checkout. Writing to a temporary file and moving it after masking would close the window; it is named for the owner of advisory items, dotfiles-T133-verdict-audit-pool-followup-a01.

P3 (high). (a) Fixed in f75cdc1f: task item 2 says every blocked request leaves <request>.rejected; d0fd7859 blocked a malformed name without one, and red test 94a9345e now requires it. (b) For the orchestrator, no code change: task item 2 still names `.claude/worktrees/orchestrator-review` and `orchestrator-review-2` as the slots, while the revise ACCEPTANCE of 20:40:19Z requires `orchestrator-audit-<n>` for every slot, which the code follows; the acceptance record should note the superseded sentence.
P3 (medium), fixed in f75cdc1f: the shdoc paragraph and `@option --json` now say the extracted record is written, masked as JSON, checked again and removed on any failure.

Revise 1: one round on d0fd7859 by a fresh read-only subagent, given the commit range, the orchestrator's local review of cfeca64 and the task file. It ran tests only in its own scratch worktrees. Verdict: correct, no P0, P1 or P2, four P3 (above). It reproduced red on b179e9c2 for all four revise tests with the intended causes and green on d0fd7859 (25 tests), confirmed every retained test name, assertion and subTest count against cfeca64 (asserts 35 to 38 and 25 to 30, subTests 12 and 7 unchanged), and found no remaining injection path from queue names. Local process evidence, not the task-level audit.
